newsitem.title: CHINA: CHINA'S LARGEST OILFIELD BOOSTS RESERVES.
newsitem.headline: CHINA'S LARGEST OILFIELD BOOSTS RESERVES.

text.p: Daqing oilfield in northeast China, the country's largest, added one billion tonnes to its reserves recently, the Xinhua news agency said on Monday.
This meant another 15 years of high yield for the three-decades-old oilfield in Heilongjiang province, it added.
Daqing's proven reserves were 5.26 billion tonnes, 4.65 billion tonnes of which have been tapped, Xinhua said.
Output broke the 50 million tonne mark in 1976. Production surged to 56 million tonnes in 1994 and has maintained that level for three years.

Production in 1996 accounted for 35.6 percent of China's total oil output. In the first six months of 1997, Daqing produced 27.79 million tonnes of oil with an industrial value of 25.3 billion yuan ($3.05 billion), Xinhua said.
Daqing aimed to become a multinational oil syndicate in the next 15 years, Xinhua said.
It hoped to boost sales and profits to three times the 1995 amount by the year 2010, it said without giving further details.
